Title: MMLongBench-Doc: Benchmarking Long-context Document Understanding with Visualizations
Problem: Long-context multimodal document understanding across charts/tables/text
Method: Evaluation benchmark with 135 long PDFs (avg 47.5 pages) and 1000+ QA pairs
Main findings: LVLMs struggle heavily with long-context cross-page reasoning (often worse than text LLMs on OCR text); 20% unanswerable questions test hallucination
Limitations: No explicit adaptive visual routing or low-level image degradation benchmark
Potential overlap: Provides long document benchmark and unanswerable question protocol
Potential novelty: Our proposed framework integrates adaptive routing and evidence grounding into retrieval-reasoning

Title: LongDocURL: a Comprehensive Multimodal Long Document Benchmark Integrating Understanding Reasoning and Locating
Problem: Evaluating multimodal long documents across understanding reasoning and locating
Method: Comprehensive benchmark with 2325 QA pairs across 33000+ pages
Main findings: Locating cross-element evidence across pages is the primary failure mode of contemporary VLMs
Limitations: Evaluation only; does not provide an adaptive mitigation or uncertainty calibration framework
Potential overlap: Benchmark overlap for long-document locating evaluation
Potential novelty: Our system adds uncertainty-guided abstention and degradation robustness

Title: XL-DocBench: Benchmarking Evidence-Grounded Extra-Long Document Understanding
Problem: Evidence-grounded extra-long document understanding up to 2303 pages
Method: Human-verified benchmark requiring models to ground answers with specific page evidence
Metrics: Answer EM / Grounding Recall@K / Page Accuracy
Main findings: 72.6% of questions require multi-page evidence; VLMs degrade severely as page count increases
Limitations: Focuses on clean scanned/digital pages without real-world visual corruptions
Potential overlap: Benchmark overlap for evidence grounding in long documents
Potential novelty: We study grounding stability under visual degradation with uncertainty-aware abstention

Title: ColPali: Efficient Document Retrieval with Vision Language Models
Problem: Bypassing brittle OCR pipelines for document retrieval using multimodal embeddings
Method: Late-interaction multi-vector patch embeddings based on PaliGemma architecture
Main findings: VLM patch embeddings dramatically outperform text-only retrieval on visual/table layouts
Limitations: High index storage footprint; does not quantify degradation impact or calibrated abstention
Relation to Gap 2: Direct (multimodal page/patch retrieval for long documents)
Relation to Gap 3: Partial (visual retrieval tested on complex layouts)
Potential novelty: We integrate multimodal retrieval with adaptive degradation routing and calibrated abstention

Title: DocVQA: A Dataset for VQA on Document Images
Problem: Visual question answering on single-page document images
Method: Benchmark dataset with 50000 questions over 12000 document images
Main findings: Standard for document QA; layout and visual structure are critical for information extraction
Limitations: Single-page focus; clean/moderately scanned documents without systematic degradation levels
Potential novelty: We extend beyond single-page clean QA to long-document degraded adaptive processing

Title: FUNSD: A Dataset for Form Understanding in Noisy Scanned Documents
Problem: Spatial and textual understanding in degraded noisy scanned forms
Method: 199 scanned forms with key-value pair and entity linking annotations
Main findings: Visual noise and poor scan quality degrade spatial OCR and entity grouping significantly
Limitations: Small dataset; single-page only; no abstention evaluation
Potential novelty: We benchmark degradation curves systematically rather than treating noise as static

Title: Selective 'Selective Prediction': Reducing Unnecessary Abstention in Vision-Language Reasoning
Problem: Over-cautious abstention in vision-language models causing low coverage
Method: Active clue retrieval and multi-step reasoning before deciding to abstain (ReCoVERR)
Main findings: Static threshold abstention throws away correctable answers; active evidence gathering boosts coverage
Limitations: Evaluated on general images rather than complex multi-page documents
Potential overlap: Algorithmic overlap in selective prediction and abstention
Potential novelty: We formulate abstention specifically for document processing with visual degradation

Title: Variational Visual Question Answering for Uncertainty-Aware Selective Prediction
Problem: Estimating predictive uncertainty in VQA without heavy Monte Carlo sampling
Method: Variational Bayes formulation over VLM representation space for calibrated selective prediction
Main findings: Variational representations yield better calibrated uncertainty than softmax temperature scaling
Limitations: General natural images only; not applied to document tables or multi-page PDF retrieval
Relation to Gap 1: Direct (uncertainty estimation and selective prediction in VLMs)
Potential novelty: We combine multimodal evidence support with visual quality vectors for document calibration

Title: Learning Conformal Abstention Policies for Adaptive Risk Management in Large Language and Vision-Language Models
Problem: Guaranteeing finite-sample risk bounds in VLM decision making with abstention
Method: Conformal prediction combined with reinforcement learned adaptive abstention policies
Main findings: Conformal thresholds provide rigorous statistical guarantees on error rates under abstention
Limitations: Requires exchangeable validation calibration data; sensitive to distribution shifts
Potential novelty: We apply calibrated selective prediction specifically to multimodal evidence-grounded IDP

Title: Consistency and Uncertainty: Identifying Unreliable Responses From Black-Box Vision-Language Models
Problem: Uncertainty quantification in API-based black-box VLMs without logits
Method: Neighborhood consistency across visually perturbed input images and prompt variations
Main findings: Semantic answer consistency over visual neighborhoods reliably detects hallucinated answers
Limitations: Computationally expensive (multiple forward passes per query); tested on natural scenes
Potential novelty: We integrate model consistency with OCR confidence and retrieval grounding scores

Title: Benchmarking Neural Network Robustness to Common Corruptions and Perturbations
Problem: Standardizing robustness evaluation under controlled visual corruptions
Method: ImageNet-C benchmark with 15 corruption types across 5 severity levels
Main findings: Neural networks experience catastrophic accuracy drop under mild common corruptions (blur/noise/compression)
Limitations: Designed for natural object classification; lacks document-specific corruptions (skew/cutoff/glare)
Relation to Gap 3: Direct (establishes standard multi-severity corruption grid methodology)
Potential overlap: Methodological foundation for controlled degradation benchmark
Potential novelty: We adapt the multi-severity corruption protocol to document structures and VLM text extraction

Title: DocTr: Document Image Restoration with Transformers
Problem: Restoring degraded document images (geometric distortion and illumination artifacts)
Method: Transformer-based geometric rectification and illumination correction network
Main findings: Deep geometric and illumination restoration significantly improves OCR word accuracy
Limitations: Heavy compute overhead; can introduce synthetic artifacts or blur text strokes if applied blindly
Potential novelty: We use adaptive routing so enhancement is applied only to moderately degraded documents

Title: Consensus Entropy: Training-Free Multi-VLM Agreement for Document OCR Verification
Problem: Verifying text recognition in complex and degraded documents without retraining
Method: Consensus entropy computed over predictions of diverse lightweight and heavy VLMs
Main findings: Multi-model agreement provides high-precision signal for recognizing when OCR is erroneous
Limitations: Requires multiple model calls; lacks formal abstention policy and evidence grounding
Relation to Gap 3: Direct (applied to complex and degraded documents)
Potential novelty: We incorporate multi-signal agreement into a unified calibrated uncertainty estimator

Title: Grounding-DocVQA: Toward Visually Grounded Document Question Answering
Problem: Evaluating whether document VQA models can locate the visual evidence justifying their answers
Method: Annotated subset of DocVQA with ground-truth bounding box evidence annotations
Main findings: Over 40% of correct answers from standard models are based on spurious correlations without visual grounding
Limitations: Single-page documents only; no adaptive processing for corrupted documents
Relation to Gap 2: Direct (evaluates spatial evidence grounding in documents)
Potential overlap: Evidence grounding protocol for document VQA
Potential novelty: We extend grounding evaluation to multi-page long documents under systematic degradation

Title: DocGround: Large-Scale Document Visual Grounding for Intelligent Document Processing
Problem: Dense spatial grounding of arbitrary queries and answers in complex documents
Method: Pretrained visual grounding head for document tokens with bounding box coordinates
Main findings: Explicit spatial grounding tokens improve answer faithfulness and reduce hallucinated entities by 28%
Limitations: Evaluated on clean documents; does not provide uncertainty calibration or abstention policies
Potential novelty: We link grounding confidence directly to our uncertainty estimation and abstention mechanism
